memoryText: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Mark 1:15 slowly, several times, and say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
These are the first recorded words of Jesus’ public ministry in Mark, and they sum up his whole message.

“The time is fulfilled.” The waiting is over. For centuries the prophets had promised a day when God would rescue his people and rule. That day has arrived. Everything in the Old Testament was moving toward this moment.

“And the kingdom of God is at hand.” The kingdom is God’s reign. It is near, not as an idea, but as a person. The King is standing in Galilee.

“Repent.” To repent is to change direction, to turn from sin and self toward God. It is not just feeling sorry. It is a change of mind that leads to a change of life.

“And believe in the gospel.” To believe is to trust. The gospel is the good news that the King has come to save. The proper response to good news is to receive it with trust.

Notice the two verbs go together. We repent and believe. They are two sides of one turning. This is how a Christian life begins, and it is how it continues.

When you wonder where to begin each day, say this verse. Turn to him again.
weekInReview: This week you began the Gospel of Mark, the fast-moving account of the servant King. In chapter 1 you saw Jesus baptized, tempted, and announcing that the kingdom of God is at hand. Your doctrinal pause on the kingdom taught you to see it as already here and not yet complete. In chapters 2 and 3 he forgave a paralyzed man, ate with sinners, and said new wine needs new wineskins. In chapters 4 to 6 you watched him teach about the seed, still a storm, free a demoniac, raise Jairus’s daughter, be rejected in Nazareth, and feed five thousand. Psalm 107 helped you hear the stilling of the storm as the LORD’s own work. Through it all, Mark kept asking who this is.
reflectionQuestions: Jesus began his ministry with the words “Repent and believe in the gospel.” What does repenting and believing look like in the details of your life this week?
The kingdom is both already here and not yet complete. Where do you see signs of it now, and where are you still waiting?
The disciples asked “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” How would you answer that question after what you have read this week?
prayerPrompts: Repent and believe the gospel, in your own words.
